research_question: What are the authoritative, teachable principles for interaction feedback and UI state coverage — visibility of system status, feedback for every action (no silent actions), and the full set of component/page states (default, hover, focus, active, loading, empty, error, success, disabled), plus microinteractions and response-time thresholds — such that an AI designer agent can apply them directly in a Next/Tailwind/Radix/shadcn substrate and a vision-capable review gauntlet can mechanically PASS/FAIL a rendered UI against them?

phases.name: Landscape
phases.objective: Survey the consensus: Nielsen's #1 heuristic (visibility of system status), the canonical UI state set (the 'five states' / default-loading-empty-error-success + interactive states), microinteraction structure (trigger -> rules -> feedback -> loops), and the response-time / Doherty-threshold model.
sub_questions: How do authoritative sources (NN/g visibility-of-system-status & microinteractions, Refactoring UI empty states, the 'states of a component' canon) enumerate the required states for components and pages?
What are the established response-time thresholds (Doherty <400ms; NN/g 0.1s/1s/10s limits) and how do they dictate WHEN to show immediate vs progress vs background feedback?
phases.evidence_priorities: NN/g visibility of system status; NN/g response-time limits (0.1/1/10s); NN/g microinteractions; Refactoring UI empty states; the canonical component-states list. Cite primary/authoritative sources.
phases.stop_condition: Complete when the full state set, the feedback heuristic, the microinteraction model, and the response-time thresholds are each documented from a primary source.

phases.name: Mechanics
phases.objective: Document how feedback and states are implemented and reasoned about: every interactive element exposes hover/focus/active/disabled visually; async actions show loading (spinner/skeleton/progress) and resolve to success or error; lists/data have an empty state; forms validate inline; the no-silent-action rule; optimistic UI; aria-live for status; focus management. Map to which feedback fits which latency.
sub_questions: What is the complete checklist of states a component/page must cover (interactive states + async/data states), and what is the rule that EVERY user action gets visible feedback within the appropriate time?

How are states implemented checkably in a component substrate (loading skeletons, disabled state with non-color signifier, error state color+icon+text, empty-state with guidance) and surfaced to assistive tech (aria-live, role=status, aria-disabled)?
phases.evidence_priorities: Microinteraction trigger/feedback model; loading/skeleton/optimistic-UI patterns; empty-state anatomy; inline-validation guidance; ARIA live regions / status roles. Concrete, checkable forms.
phases.stop_condition: Complete when the state checklist, the no-silent-action feedback rule, and the assistive-tech status pattern are each documented with a citable source and a concrete checkable form.

phases.name: Failure Modes
phases.objective: Catalog how feedback/state coverage breaks and how each reads to the user and is detected: silent actions (click with no response), missing loading state (frozen UI / double-submit), missing empty state (blank screen), unstyled/absent error state, no visible focus, color-only state, disabled control that looks enabled, console errors that break render, state-transition flicker/FOUC.
sub_questions: What are the most common, highest-impact feedback/state defects, and how does each manifest to the user (uncertainty, perceived freeze, blank screen, lost action, ambiguous state)?

How can each defect be DETECTED from a rendered page — clicking a control and observing no DOM/visual change, no loading indicator on async, empty container with no empty-state, error path with no styled error, missing focus ring, console errors, layout shift/flicker on transition?
phases.evidence_priorities: NN/g status/feedback failures; empty-state anti-patterns; double-submit/loading issues; FOUC/CLS as a feedback failure; console-error-breaks-render. For each, an observed-vs-expected detection method.
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 7+ distinct feedback/state failure modes are documented, each with a user-visible symptom AND a programmatic detection method.

phases.name: Contrarian
phases.objective: Surface nuance: over-feedback (too many toasts/spinners), spinner vs skeleton vs optimistic tradeoffs, when NOT to block on a spinner, Zeigarnik/goal-gradient effects, and reduced-motion constraints on feedback animation.
sub_questions: When does feedback become noise or harm (excessive notifications, spinner-for-fast-actions, motion that violates prefers-reduced-motion), and how should a teachable rule calibrate feedback to latency and importance rather than feeding back on everything?
phases.evidence_priorities: Critiques of over-notification; spinner-vs-skeleton-vs-optimistic debates; perceived-performance; prefers-reduced-motion for feedback. Note settled vs contextual.
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 2+ substantive critiques/nuances of naive feedback-everything are documented with the recommended hedge.

search_strategy: Nielsen visibility of system status heuristic feedback
five states of a component empty loading error success
microinteractions trigger rules feedback loops Saffer
empty state design pattern guidance Refactoring UI
skeleton screen vs spinner perceived performance
inline form validation error message pattern
aria-live role status assistive technology feedback
visible focus indicator state hover active disabled
exclusion_criteria: Tool/SaaS tutorials (how to use a specific prototyping product)
Framework-specific API docs without principle content
Pre-2017 articles superseded by modern async-UI practice

required_output_schema.per_finding_format: claim, supporting evidence, confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), source URLs, counter-evidence if any

openai_instructions: Focus on the canonical state checklist and the exact response-time thresholds (0.1s instant, 1s flow, 10s attention limit; Doherty <400ms). Build a fault tree of feedback/state failures, each with a programmatic detection method (click -> no DOM/visual delta = silent action; async with no loading node; empty container with no empty-state element; error path with no styled error; missing :focus-visible ring; color-only state; console error present; layout shift on transition). Deductive and precise; prefer NN/g and primary sources.
gemini_instructions: SKIP — Gemini engine disabled for this run.
claude_instructions: Investigate the contrarian angle (over-feedback, spinner-vs-skeleton-vs-optimistic, reduced-motion), cross-verify the response-time thresholds and the visibility-of-system-status heuristic against NN/g primary text, and confirm the canonical state set. Verify aria-live/role=status is the normative pattern for announcing async status to assistive tech.
